items.title: WPL gene order
items.description: States that the gene sequence for the first scenario is WPL (or L–P–W), with P located in the middle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires concluding the order of W, P, L; reference states 'the gene sequence is WPL.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a wrong order such as W–L–P or fails to commit to an order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to first sub-question; 0/2 discrimination but correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States gene sequence is WPL with P in middle.

items.title: W-L flanking genes
items.description: Identifies W and L as the flanking (outer) genes in the first scenario because W and L are never cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference concludes W–L are not cotransduced so they exceed the packaging limit and must be the outer pair.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places W and L adjacent or fails to use their non-cotransduction to identify them as outer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning supporting the WPL order; 0/2 discrimination but load-bearing for the conclusion.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Identifies A and C as the flanking (outer) genes in the second scenario because A and C are only infrequently cotransduced.

validation.gold_why: W and L not cotransduced, flanking P in WPL order.

items.title: ABC gene order
items.description: States that the gene sequence for the second scenario is ABC (or C–B–A), with B in the middle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) asks about relative position of A, B, C; reference states 'the sequence is ABC.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the ABC order cannot be determined or leaves part (b) without a committed order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to second sub-question; 0/2 discrimination but correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: States the sequence is ABC with B in middle.

items.title: ABC order definitive
items.description: Concludes the ABC gene order as a definitive result rather than hedging it as tentative or uncertain.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 hedged the ABC inference as 'less certain'; reference treats ABC as definitive with a mechanistic explanation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly states ABC but adds a caveat that the inference is weaker or less certain than the WPL conclusion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; distinguishes a correct definitive claim from a hedged non-answer.

validation.gold_why: States 'the sequence is ABC' definitively.

items.title: Phage carries small piece
items.description: States that the phage vector can carry only a small piece of the donor chromosome to the cell about to be transduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference opens with 'the phage vector can carry only a small piece of the donor chromosome to the cell about to be transduced.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives orders and the 2% value but never states the basic mechanism of transducing phage packaging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; general context, less specific than the 2 percent packaging limit.

validation.gold_why: States phage carries only a small piece of donor chromosome.

items.title: 2% genome packaging limit
items.description: States that only about 2 percent of the E. coli genome can fit into a transducing phage.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference cites 'only about 2 percent of the E. coli genome can fit into a transducing phage'; no rollout included this value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives correct orders but never cites the physical packaging limit that grounds the reasoning.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific quantitative anchor essential to the distance reasoning.

validation.gold_why: States about 2 percent of E. coli genome fits in phage.

items.title: Closely linked cotransduce
items.description: States that only closely linked genes can be cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'only genes that are closely linked can be cotransduced'; rollouts omitted this general framing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to specific orders without stating the general condition for cotransduction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; general principle, near-duplicate of the more specific 2 percent items.

validation.gold_why: States only closely linked genes can be cotransduced.

items.title: Genes >2% not cotransduced
items.description: States that genes separated by more than about 2 percent of the total chromosome will not be cotransduced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'Genes that are separated by a length of DNA that comprises more than about 2 percent of the total chromosome will not be cotransduced.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that cites the 2% packaging limit but does not state its consequence for cotransduction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; direct consequence of the packaging limit that explains the W-L result.

validation.gold_why: States genes separated by more than 2 percent won't cotransduce.

items.title: W-P and P-L within 2%
items.description: States that W and P, and P and L, are close enough to be located on a piece of E. coli chromosome that is less than 2 percent of the total length.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'W and P, and P and L, can be cotransduced, so we conclude that they are close enough to be located on a piece of E. coli chromosome that is less than 2 percent.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that only discusses the non-cotransduced pair without applying the 2% limit to the cotransducible pairs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; explains why both adjacent pairs cotransduce and supports P in the middle.

validation.gold_why: States W-P and P-L are within 2 percent limit.

items.title: W-L exceeds 2% limit
items.description: States that the W–L distance exceeds the 2 percent limit of the chromosome segment a phage can carry.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the segment of chromosome that carries both W and L must exceed the 2 percent limit.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that says W–L are far apart but does not connect their non-cotransduction to exceeding the packaging limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; explains the non-cotransduction of W and L and justifies P as middle gene.

validation.gold_why: States W-L segment must exceed the 2 percent limit.

items.title: A-C near 2% limit
items.description: States that the A–C distance is close to but within the 2 percent limit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the A—C distance is less than that of the W—L region and is close to the 2 percent limit.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the ABC order but does not explain why A–C is infrequent rather than never cotransduced.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; positions A–C near the packaging boundary, explaining infrequent cotransduction.

validation.gold_why: States A-C distance is close to the 2 percent limit.

items.title: A-C less than W-L
items.description: States that the A–C distance is less than the W–L distance.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly compares: 'the A—C distance is less than that of the W—L region.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both parts as analogous without distinguishing the physical difference between 'never' and 'infrequently.'
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; comparative insight linking the two scenarios, but secondary to the orders.

validation.gold_why: States A-C distance is less than W-L distance.

items.title: Breaks outside A and C
items.description: Explains that infrequent A–C cotransduction requires chromosomal breaks immediately outside both A and C loci.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the breaks in the chromosome would have to be immediately outside the two loci, and this can only be expected to occur rarely.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains infrequency only qualitatively as 'larger distance' without the break-position mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; mechanistic explanation for why A–C cotransduction is infrequent.

validation.gold_why: Breaks must be immediately outside both loci, occurring rarely.

items.title: Rare breaks cause infrequency
items.description: States that these required chromosomal breaks outside A and C can only be expected to occur rarely, leading to the observed infrequent cotransduction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference states 'the breaks in the chromosome would have to be immediately outside the two loci, and this can only be expected to occur rarely.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains infrequency only qualitatively as 'larger distance' without the break-position mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Measured as part of source 10 (2/2 negatives); completes the mechanistic chain for the second scenario.

validation.gold_why: Breaks must be immediately outside both loci, occurring rarely.

validation.gold_why: Divides by 5, does not multiply

items.title: Avoid M1V1=M2V2

validation.gold_why: Uses normality equation, not M1V1=M2V2

items.description: The response writes the probability of getting eigenvalue E_k as |⟨E_k|ψ(t)⟩|² = |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|², using the time-evolution operator U(t) and the relation |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; highest discrimination, directly answers the question.

validation.gold_why: Final boxed expression equals |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|².

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate form; required to derive the phase factor.

items.title: Eigenvalue equation used
items.description: The response uses the energy eigenvalue equation H|E_k⟩ = E_k|E_k⟩ to evaluate the action of the time-evolution operator on the eigenstate |E_k⟩.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing step connecting Hamiltonian eigenstates to U(t) action.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the second sub-question; states the required conclusion.

items.title: General initial state
items.description: The response carries out the derivation for a general initial state |ψ(0)⟩ at time t, not only for the special case |ψ(0)⟩ = |E_k⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The eigenstate-only proof pitfall (severity medium) warns against proving the result only for the trivial case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.

items.title: Avoids amplitude-as-probability
items.description: Avoids stating or implying that the probability is the unsquared amplitude e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩, instead taking the modulus squared of the full amplitude.

provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the amplitude with its time-dependent phase and concludes the probability is time-dependent because the phase survives.

validation.gold_why: Uses modulus squared, not unsquared amplitude.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/2 negatives; specific algebraic mistake observed in flawed responses.

validation.gold_why: No incorrect z·z evaluation present.

items.title: Boltzmann probability W_n
items.description: The response writes the probability of the state with n open links at equilibrium as W_n = (1/Z) exp{−nΔ/T} with Z = Σ_{n=0}^{N} exp{−nΔ/T}.

items.description: The response states the final result \(dS = \frac{dV_B}{T}(P_B - P_A)\) for the two-compartment system, with the common temperature \(T\) in the denominator and no residual \(dU_A\) or \(dU_B\) term.

validation.gold_why: Per-subsystem entropy relation written.

validation.gold_why: First-law heat expressions written.

items.title: Volume conservation constraint

validation.gold_why: Uses dV_A = -dV_B.

items.title: Energy conservation constraint

validation.gold_why: dU_A = -dU_B applied.

items.title: Equal temperatures used

items.title: Total entropy as sum

validation.gold_why: Writes √(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²), an equivalent form.

items.title: Prefactor N/π, a cancels
items.description: The final expression for n(E) has the prefactor N/π with no spurious factor of a, because the measure dk = dx/a from the substitution x = ka cancels the prefactor a in Na/π.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed the lattice constant a cancels via dk=dx/a, leaving N/π.
provenance.discriminates: A response that retains a spurious factor of a in the prefactor, giving 2Na/(π√(…)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged with lattice-constant item; caught 2/2 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: No factor of a; prefactor simplifies to 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−Es)²)).

items.title: Change of variable
items.description: The response performs the change of variable x = ka so that dk = dx/a and the integral limits transform from [−π/a, π/a] to [−π, π].

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate step enabling the cancellation of a and the delta identity.

items.title: Transformed integral form
items.description: The response writes the transformed integral as (N/π)∫_{−π}^{π} δ(E−E_s+2J cos x) dx after the substitution, showing the prefactor a has cancelled.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Verifies both substitution and cancellation; specific intermediate result.

items.title: Delta function identity
items.description: The response applies the Dirac delta function identity δ(f(x)) = Σ_i δ(x−x_i)/|f'(x_i)|, where x_i are the roots of f(x) = E−E_s+2J cos x within the integration range.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core mathematical technique transforming the delta integral into algebraic terms.

items.title: Root condition
items.description: The response identifies the root condition as cos(x_i) = (E_s−E)/(2J), requiring |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J| for real solutions to exist.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate linking the cos argument to the band-support condition.

items.title: Derivative magnitude
items.description: The response computes |f'(x_i)| = |2J sin(x_i)| = 2|J|√(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²), converting the delta function contribution into a sqrt denominator involving cos.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate: produces the square-root denominator in the final expression.

items.title: Two roots accounted
items.description: The response accounts for two roots of f(x) = E−E_s+2J cos x within [−π, π], each contributing a factor 1/|f'(x_i)| to the integral.

provenance.calibration_rationale: The factor of 2 in the numerator is essential to the correct expression and easily missed.

items.title: Band edges defined
items.description: The response defines the band edges as E_b = E_s − 2|J| and E_t = E_s + 2|J|, which serve as the arguments of the Heaviside function in the final expression.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Anchors the theta arguments; specific intermediate quantity in the derivation.

items.title: Delta-to-theta explanation
items.description: The response explains that the integral of the delta function is transformed into terms involving theta because the delta has support only when |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J|, and the Heaviside function enforces this band condition.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses the second sub-question about how delta integral becomes theta terms.

items.title: Zero outside band
items.description: The response states that n(E) = 0 outside the band where |E−E_s| > 2|J|, because the delta function argument E−E_s+2J cos(ka) has no real root.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Consequence of the theta support; reinforces the physical meaning of the Heaviside factor.

items.title: Avoids reversed theta
items.description: Avoids reversing the inequality in the theta argument, e.g., writing θ((E−E_s)²−4J²) instead of θ(4J²−(E−E_s)²), which would make n(E) nonzero outside the band and zero inside.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Wrong θ support argument' (high severity): sign errors in squaring or inequality direction are common.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the support factor with the inequality reversed, inverting the band.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed trap; 0/2 discrimination on tests but a common sign error in theta form.

validation.gold_why: Theta arguments give correct nonzero-inside-band region.

items.title: Avoids single-root error
items.description: Avoids counting only one root of cos(x) = (E_s−E)/(2J) within [−π, π], which would omit the factor of 2 in the numerator of the final expression.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Common derivation error producing half the correct prefactor in the expression.

items.title: Imaginary-time exponent

items.title: Real part of saddle-point time
items.description: The response identifies the real part of the complex saddle-point time as the laser phase or continuum birth time that determines the final electron momentum.

items.title: Under-barrier time interpretation
items.description: The response discusses the relation between the imaginary part of the complex saddle-point time and the time spent under the barrier, stating that the imaginary-time interval is a formal semiclassical parameter that does not uniquely map to a real measurable tunneling time.

provenance.evidence_detail: High-severity pitfall 'Imaginary time as real dwell time': asserting Im(t_s) is a directly observable real tunneling time without caveats.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims τ_s = √(2I_p)/F is directly the physical time the electron spends under the barrier with no qualification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; core disputed point of the question on time spent under the barrier. gold=FAIL caps weight.

validation.gold_why: Mentions under-barrier time but no formal non-measurability caveat.

items.title: Steepest-descent prefactor
items.description: The response includes the Gaussian steepest-descent prefactor [2π/(±iS''(t_s))]^{1/2} in the expression for the ionization amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent claim: rollouts disagreed on the sign of i in the prefactor ([2π/(-iS'')]^{1/2} vs [2π/(iS'')]^{1/2}), which is convention-dependent on contour orientation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the Gaussian prefactor entirely, leaving only the exponential part of the saddle-point approximation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives but a technical detail beyond the core derivation; gold=FAIL and low importance.

items.title: Second derivative of action
items.description: The response gives the second derivative of the action at the complex saddle-point time as S''(t_s) = ±(p ± A(t_s))·E(t_s), consistent with the chosen sign convention.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent claim: rollouts differed on the overall sign due to the p+A vs p-A convention, but both are internally consistent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes S'' = k·E with a sign inconsistent with its own definition of k = p±A.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 2/2 negatives; required intermediate quantity for the steepest-descent prefactor. gold=FAIL limits weight.

validation.gold_why: No second derivative of action given.

items.description: Computes the rates r1 = 1.0 mmHg/sec and r2 = 0.26 mmHg/sec by dividing each pressure drop by the time of 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: r1 = (300 − 400)/100 = 1, equivalently r1 = x1/t = 100/100 = 1.0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong time interval or miscalculates the rate would produce a different r1, affecting the order determination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate for order determination but follows directly from x values. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: r1=1 computed as 100/100.

items.title: Order formula
items.description: Applies the differential order formula n = log(r1/r2) / log(a1/a2) using initial pressures a1 = 400 and a2 = 200 as the concentration terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: n = ln(r1/r2) / ln(a1/a2) with a1 = 400 and a2 = 200.
provenance.discriminates: A response using remaining pressures (300 and 174) instead of initial pressures (400 and 200) as concentration terms would get n ≈ 2.5 instead of ≈ 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key method for determining order from two experiments. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Applies n=ln(r1/r2)/ln(a1/a2).

items.title: Order n ≈ 2
items.description: Reports the reaction order n as approximately 2 with respect to CH3CHO, the primary asked quantity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: n = ln(1/0.26)/ln(400/200) ≈ 1.94, rounded to 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response with incorrect intermediate values would produce a different order (e.g., 1.5 or 2.5).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the first sub-question; correctness collapses without it. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Reports n≈1.94, rounds to 2.

items.title: Second-order rate law
items.description: Applies the second-order integrated rate law k = (1/t) · x / [a(a − x)] for calculating the rate constant, where a is the initial pressure and (a − x) is the remaining pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses k = (1/t) · x / [a(a−x)], the second-order integrated rate law in pressure units.
provenance.discriminates: A response using the first-order law k = (1/t)·ln[a/(a−x)] or zero-order k = x/t would produce k values off by orders of magnitude with wrong units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct rate law selection is essential for k computation. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses k=(1/t)·x/[a(a−x)].

items.title: k1 and k2 from both experiments
items.description: Computes k1 = 8.33 × 10⁻⁶ and k2 = 7.47 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ separately from both experiments (P0 = 400 with remaining 300, and P0 = 200 with remaining 174) using t = 100 sec.

provenance.discriminates: A response using the wrong rate law or wrong x would obtain a different k1 value or different units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Both k values are required before averaging; merges both-experiments requirement. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: k1=8.33e-6 from experiment 1.

items.title: Average k = 7.9e-6
items.description: Reports the average rate constant k at 500°C as 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ obtained by averaging the k values from both experiments.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: k_av = 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports only one k value or an incorrect average would not match this final rate constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the second sub-question. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Average k=7.9e-6 reported.

items.title: T1 = 773 K
items.description: Converts the temperature 500°C to 773 K for use as T1 in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: T1 = 773 K (or 773.15 K) used in Arrhenius calculation.
provenance.discriminates: A response plugging 500 directly into the Arrhenius equation would obtain a nonsensical T2 ≈ 503 K.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Simple but necessary conversion for Arrhenius calculation. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses 773 K as T1.

items.title: Ea = 180000 J, R = 8.314
items.description: Converts activation energy of 180 kJ to 180000 J and uses R = 8.314 J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses 180000 in the Arrhenius calculation with R = 8.314.
provenance.discriminates: A response using Ea = 180 directly with R = 8.314 would produce a temperature essentially unchanged from T1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Unit-consistent parameters are required for correct Arrhenius result. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Uses 180000 J for Ea.

items.title: ln 2 as k ratio
items.description: Uses ln 2 as the ratio k2/k1 in the two-point Arrhenius equation, since the rate constant is to be twice its value at 500°C.

provenance.discriminates: A response using a different ratio (e.g., ln 1 = 0, or 2 instead of ln 2) would solve for a different T2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key setup for the temperature sub-question; incorrect ratio gives wrong T2. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: ln 2 used as k ratio.

items.title: T2 ≈ 793 K
items.description: Reports the final temperature T2 as approximately 793 K (≈ 520°C) at which the rate constant is twice its 500°C value.

provenance.discriminates: A response with a sign error in the Arrhenius equation would obtain T2 < 773 K, and one using Celsius or unconverted Ea would obtain entirely different values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers third sub-question; highest measured discrimination, caught 2/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: T2≈793 K (520°C) reported.

items.title: k units mmHg⁻¹s⁻¹
items.description: Avoids reporting the second-order rate constant k without units, correctly stating mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹ consistent with pressure data used.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Rate-constant units mismatch': solvers may report k in s⁻¹ (first-order) or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ instead of mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response reporting k in s⁻¹ or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ units would be dimensionally inconsistent with the second-order pressure-based derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common unit pitfall for second-order pressure-based k; caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: k units given as mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.

items.title: Unrounded n ≈ 1.94
items.description: Reports the unrounded value of the reaction order as approximately 1.94 (or 1.943) before rounding to 2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference reports n = 1.9434165 ≈ 2; the intermediate unrounded value confirms the differential method was actually applied.
provenance.discriminates: A response that simply states n = 2 without showing the computed value ~1.94 may have guessed the order rather than deriving it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added depth showing the raw computation result before rounding. Caught 1/2 negatives.

validation.gold_why: Reports 1.9434165 before rounding.

items.title: Core formula
items.description: Presents the expression $\|P_0\|^2 + 2 \cdot (D_1 + D_2) \cdot t$ as the result for the change in distance between the two Brownian particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts used coefficient 6 for the diffusion term in three dimensions, while the reference uses coefficient 2.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives, gold=pass; the formula is the answer's backbone.

validation.gold_why: Expression presented verbatim in the answer.

items.title: Initial separation P0
items.description: Defines $P_0$ as the initial separation vector $P_1 - P_2$ between the two particles at their starting coordinates.

items.title: Second-moment label
items.description: Identifies the expression $\|P_0\|^2 + 2 \cdot (D_1 + D_2) \cdot t$ as the second moment $E[|R(t)|^2]$ of the relative displacement of the two particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: The analysis flags divergence in what quantity the reference formula represents; labeling it correctly as a second moment distinguishes it from variance or mean.

items.title: Avoid vector shortcut

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Scalar distance vs vector' pitfall (severity high) warns that treating distance as displacement yields zero mean and misses the nonlinear |·| treatment.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports E[Δx] = 0 and Var[Δx] = 2(D1+D2)t per coordinate, treating the vector displacement as the answer to a scalar-distance question.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/3 negatives; real conceptual trap tied to scalar-vs-vector confusion.

validation.gold_why: Answer does not interpret change as vector with zero mean.

items.description: States that the velocity distribution remains a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at the initial temperature T after infinite time.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts predicted T∞ < T or T∞ → 0, contradicting the reference which says the distribution remains MB at initial T.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Core correct answer; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

items.title: Final temperature equals T
items.description: States that the final temperature after infinite time equals the initial temperature T (i.e., T∞ = T).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverged on T∞ values of ≤T, <T, or indeterminate; reference definitively states T∞ = T.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that claim the gas cools to a reduced terminal temperature or heats from recoil.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core numerical result; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Implies final temperature equals initial T.

items.title: Avoids radiative cooling

provenance.calibration_rationale: Primary observed trap; caught 3/3 negatives, discrimination 1.00.

validation.gold_why: Does not claim T∞ < T or T∞ → 0.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Key mechanistic error; caught 2/3 negatives, discrimination 0.67.

validation.gold_why: No one-way collisional cooling claim.
